name: Astro
subtitle: Content-focused framework (islands)
creator: Fred K. Schott and team
description: A framework that ships zero JavaScript by default. Pages render to HTML at build time or on the server, and only interactive islands (components from React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and others) load in the browser. Content Collections give type-safe Markdown or CMS content.

languages.youWrite: .astro files (frontmatter plus a JSX-like template), Markdown and MDX

concepts.explanation: Interactive components hydrate independently on a static page.
Pages are plain HTML unless you opt in.
client:load, client:visible and client:idle control hydration.
Schema-validated Markdown, MDX or CMS content.
Switch from static output to on-demand rendering.
Render dynamic parts of a page separately on the server.

codeSamples.label: Astro · src/pages/index.astro

pros: Top-tier performance and Core Web Vitals
Use any UI framework, or several at once
Highest satisfaction of any meta-framework in State of JS 2025 (94%)
cons: Not ideal for highly interactive, app-like products
Sharing state between islands takes extra work
Some worry about a Cloudflare bias, though both companies have committed to portability

surveys.source: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, all respondents
